skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.summary: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

skills.name: implement-spec
skills.summary: Implement a specification in code.

skills.name: implement
skills.summary: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.summary: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

skills.name: prototype
skills.summary: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

skills.name: research
skills.summary: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

skills.name: retro
skills.summary: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

skills.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
skills.summary: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

skills.name: tdd
skills.summary: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

skills.name: to-spec
skills.summary: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

skills.name: to-tickets
skills.summary: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

skills.name: triage
skills.summary: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

skills.name: wayfinder
skills.summary: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

skills.name: wizard
skills.summary: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

skills.name: claude-handoff
skills.summary: Hand the current conversation off to a fresh background agent that picks up the work immediately.

skills.name: loop-me
skills.summary: Grill me about specs for the workflows I want to build, within this workspace.

skills.name: setup-ts-deep-modules
skills.summary: Wire dependency-cruiser into a TypeScript repo so each package is a deep module, with implementation hidden in subfolders and reachable only through its entry-point files. User-invoked.

skills.name: writing-beats
skills.summary: Writing, exploit; assemble raw material into a journey of beats, grounding each term before a beat leans on it.

skills.name: writing-fragments
skills.summary: Writing, explore: mine raw fragments, no structure yet.

skills.name: writing-shape
skills.summary: Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph.

skills.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
skills.summary: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.

skills.name: migrate-to-shoehorn
skills.summary: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.

skills.name: scaffold-exercises
skills.summary: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.

skills.name: setup-pre-commit
skills.summary: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.summary: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

skills.name: grilling
skills.summary: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

skills.name: handoff
skills.summary: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

skills.name: teach
skills.summary: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

skills.name: to-questionnaire
skills.summary: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

skills.name: wait-what
skills.summary: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

skills.name: writing-for-agents
skills.summary: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

skills.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
skills.summary: 按双方变更意图处理进行中的 Git merge/rebase 冲突，并执行项目检查。保留的 Matt Pocock 历史技能，上游现已移除。
